# Use cases and triggers — link and recall

Define use cases, how to trigger them, and what to link to so the agent can **recall** the right flow or skill.

**Recall:** When the user’s goal or phrasing matches a use case below, **link** to the listed flow/skill/doc and **run** the superpowers or config flow as specified.

---

## 1. Creative / feature work (idea → done) — **superpowers**

| | |
|--|--|
| **Use case** | User has an idea, feature, or multi-step change; wants to go from idea to done and reviewed. |
| **Trigger** | “I have an idea,” “build a feature,” “add X,” “implement Y,” “run superpowers,” “plan before code,” “brainstorm then implement,” or any non-trivial creative/implementation ask. |
| **Link / recall** | **cursor-workflow-bootstrap**; LOGIC_FLOWS §2, §8, §10. **You have superpowers to run.** |
| **Run** | **brainstorming** → design doc → **writing-plans** → plan doc → **executing-plans** (or **subagent-driven-development**) → **finishing-a-development-branch** → **code-reviewer** + requesting/receiving-code-review. Use **using-cursor-skills** so applicable skills are applied. |

---

## 2. Config or content (add/change skill, agent, rule, settings)

| | |
|--|--|
| **Use case** | User wants to add or change a skill, subagent, rule, slash command, editor settings, or narrative doc; or migrate rules/commands to skills. |
| **Trigger** | “Create a skill,” “add a subagent,” “new rule,” “migrate rules to skills,” “change theme/font/settings,” “port from Claude/Codex,” “/create-skill,” “/create-subagent,” “/migrate-to-skills,” “/update-cursor-settings,” “/cursor-integration,” “/create-rule.” |
| **Link / recall** | **cursor-config-content-workflow**; LOGIC_FLOWS §1, §5; reference-resources-inventory (Config & content creation skills). |
| **Run** | Route once → invoke exactly one skill: create-skill, create-subagent, create-rule, migrate-to-skills, update-cursor-settings, cursor-integration, or narrative-blueprints. |

---

## 3. Analyze / sort / organize a batch of artifacts (zips, paths, lists)

| | |
|--|--|
| **Use case** | User has a batch of zips, paths, or a long path list and wants to analyze, understand, sort, and organize intuitively. |

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import express from "express";
import { McpServer } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js";
import { StreamableHTTPServerTransport } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/streamableHttp.js";
import {
  RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE,
  registerAppResource,
  registerAppTool,
} from "@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/server";
import { z } from "zod";
import { listPastePinboards, searchPasteItems } from "./paste-client.js";
import { redactPreview } from "./redact.js";

const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);

const bundle = readFileSync(
  require.resolve("@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/app-with-deps"),
  "utf8",
).replace(/export\{([^}]+)\};?\s*$/, (_, body: string) =>
  "globalThis.ExtApps={" +
    body
      .split(",")
      .map((pair) => {
        const [local, exported] = pair.split(" as ").map((s) => s.trim());
        return `${exported ?? local}:${local}`;
      })
      .join(",") +
    "};",
);

const pickerHtml = readFileSync(join(__dirname, "../widgets/picker.html"), "utf8").replace(
  "/*__EXT_APPS_BUNDLE__*/",
  () => bundle,
);

type PickerItem = {
  id: string;
  kind: string;
  label: string;
  sub: string;
  redacted: boolean;
  note?: string;
};

function asRecord(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> | null {
  return value !== null && typeof value === "object" && !Array.isArray(value)
    ? (value as Record<string, unknown>)
    : null;
}

function pickerPayload(items: PickerItem[], note: string, error?: string) {
  return JSON.stringify({ items, note, error });
}

function fromSearch(raw: unknown): PickerItem[] {
  const rec = asRecord(raw);
  const list = Array.isArray(raw) ? raw : Array.isArray(rec?.items) ? rec.items : [];
  return list.slice(0, 40).map((row, i) => {
    const item = asRecord(row) ?? {};
    const id = String(item.id ?? `item-${i}`);
    const type = String(item.type ?? "text");
    const preview = String(item.preview ?? item.title ?? "");
    const { preview: safe, redacted } = redactPreview(preview);
    const app = item.app ? String(item.app) : "";
    return {
      id,
      kind: "item",
      label: `${type}${app ? ` · ${app}` : ""}`,
      sub: safe || id,
      redacted,
    };
  });
}

function fromPinboards(raw: unknown): PickerItem[] {
  const rec = asRecord(raw);
  const list = Array.isArray(raw)
    ? raw
    : Array.isArray(rec?.pinboards)
      ? rec.pinboards
      : [];
  return list.map((row, i) => {
    const board = asRecord(row) ?? {};
    const id = String(board.id ?? `board-${i}`);
    const name = String(board.name ?? "Untitled");
    const count = board.itemCount ?? board.item_count ?? "";
    return {
      id,
      kind: "pinboard",
      label: name,
      sub: count === "" ? id : `${count} items · ${id}`,
      redacted: false,
    };
  });
}

function createServer(): McpServer {
  const server = new McpServer({ name: "paste-mcp", version: "0.1.0" });

  registerAppResource(server, "Paste picker", "ui://widgets/picker.html", {}, async () => ({
    contents: [
      {
        uri: "ui://widgets/picker.html",
        mimeType: RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE,
        text: pickerHtml,
      },
    ],
  }));

  registerAppTool(
    server,
    "pick_paste_item",
    {
      description:
        "Opens an interactive picker of Paste clipboard/history items. Use when the user should choose one saved item. Previews redact API-key-shaped strings. Returns JSON items for hosts without widgets.",
      inputSchema: {
        query: z.string().optional().describe("Free-text search; omit for newest items"),
        limit: z.number().int().min(1).max(40).optional(),
      },
      _meta: { ui: { resourceUri: "ui://widgets/picker.html" } },
    },
    async ({ query, limit }) => {

        const items = fromSearch(raw);
        const note = `${items.length} Paste item(s). Click one. Secrets in previews are redacted.`;
        return { content: [{ type: "text", text: pickerPayload(items, note) }] };
      } catch (err) {
        const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
        return {
          content: [
            {
              type: "text",
              text: pickerPayload([], "Paste MCP unreachable.", message),
            },
          ],
          isError: true,
        };
      }
    },
  );

#!/usr/bin/python3
"""Project hooks: keep Paste/MCP secrets and .env out of the model. Fail closed on .env reads."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def emit(obj: dict) -> None:
	sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=True) + "\n")


def read_input() -> dict:
	raw = sys.stdin.read()
	try:
		data = json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {}
		return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}
	except json.JSONDecodeError:
		return {}


def before_read(data: dict) -> dict:
	path = str(data.get("file_path") or "")
	name = Path(path).name
	if name == ".env" or name.endswith(".env") and name != ".env.example":
		return {
			"permission": "deny",
			"user_message": "Blocked reading env/secret file. Use .env.example only.",
		}
	return {"permission": "allow"}


def before_mcp(data: dict) -> dict:
	tool = str(data.get("tool_name") or "")
	raw_input = data.get("tool_input")
	text = raw_input if isinstance(raw_input, str) else json.dumps(raw_input or {})
	if tool in {"create_item", "update_item"} and (
		"sk-" in text or "Bearer " in text or "ghp_" in text
	):
		return {
			"permission": "deny",
			"user_message": "Blocked Paste create/update that looks like it contains a secret.",
			"agent_message": "Do not store API keys in Paste. Use titled identity text/link/color only.",
		}
	return {"permission": "allow"}


def after_mcp(_data: dict) -> dict:
	return {
		"additional_context": (
			"paste-mcp/Paste: summarize by id, type, title, pinboard. Never quote secret-shaped text."
		)
	}


HANDLERS = {
	"beforeReadFile": before_read,
	"beforeMCPExecution": before_mcp,
	"afterMCPExecution": after_mcp,
}


def main() -> int:
	data = read_input()
	event = str(data.get("hook_event_name") or "")
	fn = HANDLERS.get(event)
	if fn is None:
		emit({})
		return 0
	try:
		emit(fn(data))
	except Exception:
		# .env read must fail closed — deny if we crashed while handling beforeReadFile.
		if event == "beforeReadFile":
			emit({"permission": "deny", "user_message": "paste-safety hook error; blocked file read."})
		else:
			emit({})
	return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
	raise SystemExit(main())

## Security design review: Paste Cleanup

### Critical findings

1. **Ambient mutation creates a confused-deputy path.** A normal `search` or `read` must not silently grant broad edit/delete authority. The agent may classify and propose, but a deterministic policy executor must decide whether an encountered item matches a previously authorized rule. Default background authority should be limited to explicitly allowlisted organizational actions.

2. **The future mutation server would be an unauthenticated credential proxy.** [server.ts](/Users/steven/github/paste-mcp/src/server.ts:194) calls `app.listen(port)` without an explicit loopback host, while [paste-client.ts](/Users/steven/github/paste-mcp/src/paste-client.ts:8) may hold an upstream bearer token. Before exposing mutation tools, bind explicitly to `127.0.0.1` and require a local capability token for organize/destructive calls. Separate read, organize, and destructive capabilities.

3. **Hard deletion cannot honestly support undo.** Deleted text/link/color items could only be recreated with new identity and timestamps; images/files cannot be recreated through Paste MCP. Never label deletion reversible. Background mode must not hard-delete. Require exact item IDs, count, types, a fresh preview, explicit approval, and Paste’s own `confirm: true`.

4. **Undo journaling can become a second secret store.** Storing original bodies to reverse edits would duplicate API keys locally. Journals should normally contain item IDs, board IDs, action, safe fingerprints, timestamps, and inverse membership operations—not content. If content restoration is ever supported, store encrypted, permission-restricted, expiring blobs outside the repository, chat, Engram, and logs.

### High findings

5. **Stale-state races can move or overwrite changed items.** Every cleanup plan needs a snapshot fingerprint. Re-read immediately before mutation; skip on title/content/membership mismatch. After mutation, re-read and verify. Use per-item serialization and idempotent operation IDs.

6. **“Move” is non-atomic.** Implement it as destination add → verify → source remove → verify. On partial failure, retain both memberships and report it; never remove the source first.

7. **Pinboard names are not identities.** Duplicate, whitespace-damaged, or spoofed `API Keys` boards could misroute secrets. Resolve a canonical private board once by stable ID, store that ID in policy, and reject shared or ambiguous destinations.

8. **Clipboard content is untrusted prompt material.** Item text may contain instructions intended to manipulate the agent. Secret detection and standing cleanup rules must be deterministic local code. The agent receives redacted metadata, never instructions derived from item bodies.

9. **Existing hooks do not protect runtime calls.** The Cursor hook blocks secret-bearing `create_item`/`update_item`, but direct upstream calls from the runtime bypass that hook. Enforce redaction, policy, and authorization inside `paste-mcp` itself. The hook also conflicts with restoring/editing secret content, reinforcing that such edits should not be automatic.

10. **Shared boards require a hard boundary.** Current project guidance says shared boards are not writable. Background cleanup must skip them and report safe metadata only. It must not infer that “private” means secure storage or change visibility guarantees.

### Medium findings

- Regex classification has false positives and false negatives. A match may trigger an allowlisted pin/move, never deletion or content rewriting.
- Background work needs a bounded async queue, rate limits, deduplication, and recursion suppression so its own mutations do not retrigger indefinitely or delay searches.
- Errors must be sanitized; upstream responses and exception strings can contain sensitive content.
- Quarantine is organization, not security isolation. Use a private quarantine board with retention metadata, but do not describe it as revocation or secure deletion.

## Recommended authorization defaults

| Tier | Default |
|---|---|
| Observe/classify encountered items | Automatic, local, redacted |
| Add to canonical private board | Automatic only under a saved rule |
| Remove from original private board | Allowed by saved move rule after destination verification |
| Rename item/board | Preview or narrowly saved normalization rule |
| Edit content | Per-operation approval |
| Quarantine | Saved policy with retention and undo journal |
| Hard delete item/board | Fresh explicit approval only; never background |
| Shared-board mutation | Denied |

For the user’s example, a saved rule may authorize: “When an encountered item locally matches an API-key pattern, pin it to canonical private board ID X; verify; then remove it from other private boards; preserve history; disclose only item ID and category.”

## Design acceptance criteria

- Threat model covers local callers, malicious clipboard text, compromised agent, stale plans, partial upstream failure, and journal theft.
- Read, organize, and destructive tools have distinct schemas and authorization gates.
- Every mutation is tied to a policy ID or approval record.
- Plans contain stable IDs, safe fingerprints, expected pre-state, exact operations, and expiry.
- Execution revalidates pre-state and verifies post-state item by item.
- Secret values never appear in tool output, widgets, titles, logs, exceptions, reports, git, memory, or ordinary journal rows.
- Move and undo are idempotent and tested across partial failure and concurrent modification.
- Deletion is clearly marked irreversible; images/files are excluded from automatic deletion and recreation claims.
- Shared and ambiguous pinboards fail closed.
- Tests cover false-positive secrets, missed-pattern handling, duplicate board names, stale state, partial moves, replayed plans, journal redaction, prompt-injection content, and exact deletion confirmations.
- Batch reports account for every requested item as completed, skipped, conflicted, failed, or irreversible.

Review was read-only. Evidence came from the current runtime source, project hooks, skill contract, and repository status; no files were modified.
